options.title: Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal?
options.first_line: Why does Gambia sit inside Senegal, like a worm inside an apple?
options.first_frame: West Africa from above: thin red Gambia curling through green Senegal along a blue river, a small wooden boat already sailing up it, both names on the map.

options.title: Gambia is just one river and its banks
options.first_line: Gambia is a whole country built on one river, and Senegal wraps all the way round it.
options.first_frame: A boat on a wide brown river, the camera pulling up and back until the river turns into a thin red country inside green Senegal.

options.title: The country Senegal swallowed (almost)
options.first_line: Senegal wraps around Gambia on every side but the sea. So how did that happen?
options.first_frame: Green Senegal's outline closing around red Gambia like two hands, a border guard at a striped barrier on the line between them.

why: It names two places you can picture and asks a how-is-that-possible question without giving the answer, while B states the twist in title and first line and C gives away the wrap-around in its first sentence.
